verdict.summary: A tidy flat-roofed pavilion with a timber soffit, grey plinth and terrace props, but the brief's floor-to-ceiling glass is missing, so it reads as a dark generic shop rather than a modern glass café.

issues.problem: Back elevation and side walls are solid black with no glazing; floor-to-ceiling glass on two sides is absent
issues.fix: Replace the black wall infill on the front and one side with full-height glass panels (2 blocks tall per storey) between slim dark steel mullions every 2-3 blocks; keep the frame, swap the infill.

issues.problem: Sign above the entrance is a speckled brown/orange block panel that reads as a plank, not a neon sign
issues.fix: Build the sign as a raised fascia band with glowing lines (sea lantern or light-colored glass outline, with a recognisable word-shape) mounted on the soffit line, not a flat block panel.

issues.problem: Thick dark slab with a lighter grey edge band reads as a lid sitting on the box, not a thin cantilevered roof
issues.fix: Thin the roof to 1 block of cap with a 1-block dark-steel edge line, and extend the timber soffit out past the walls so the cantilever shows as a shadow line.

issues.problem: Walls and roof are near-equal visual weight, so the cantilever and open terrace side feel heavy
issues.fix: Set the glazed walls back 1-2 blocks from the roof edge so the slab appears to float over the terrace.

issues.problem: Mostly black with brown and orange accents; the glass-and-steel character the brief asks for is lost
issues.fix: Use light glass (light blue stained glass or glass panes) and light-grey concrete for the plinth and terrace edges to lift the contrast.
